the clinical features of these malformations vary with their nature, age, and the presence of other cardiovascular lesions; that the diagnosis can be made with considerable accuracy by a combination of clinical, laboratory, radiographic, and echocar-diographic studies; and that surgical correction is usually feasible and is the only definitive therapy for these patients.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of a malformative obstruction to the pulmonary venous drainage should be considered in any child with unexplained cardiomegaly and pulmonary venous hypertension, especially if there is a history of cyanosis, congestive heart failure, or a murmur of mitral stenosis or regurgitation.
